rag.description: Turn the mouse wheel inside an InvokeInputActions gesture, over an element or a viewport position. The step checks its element and numbers before anything is sent, takes flexible parameters for direction and amount, and sends real wheel input, so inner lists, lazy loading, and zoom run reliably.

qa.answer: It adds one wheel scroll to the input sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
qa.question: What does the AddScroll plugin do?

qa.answer: DeltaY and DeltaX set the scroll amount in pixels, X and Y set the place of the wheel, and OnElement with Locator names an element to scroll over. It stores no outputs.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of AddScroll?

qa.answer: It runs as an InputAction task step with the gears icon and the ActionRuleModel, only as a child rule of InvokeInputActions; the pointer position does not change where the wheel turns.
qa.question: How does AddScroll fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Scroll over an element instead of a fixed position where possible, keep the element inside the viewport, and add an AddPause after the scroll when content loads.
qa.question: What are best practices for using AddScroll?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “AddScroll” and set the amount in the argument, such as {{$ --DeltaY:600}}, with onElement for an inner list, inside the rules of InvokeInputActions.
qa.question: How is an AddScroll rule configured?

qa.answer: A missing element or a value that is not a whole number fails the step, and the container then sends nothing. Outside InvokeInputActions the step fails with a message that names the container.

description: ### Purpose
AddScroll turns the mouse wheel as one action of a gesture.
It runs only inside InvokeInputActions, and the wheel turns over an element or over a point of the viewport.
Flows use it to scroll a list inside a page, to load more items, and to zoom a map or a chart that listens to the wheel.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature | Description |
| Both axes | Scrolls vertically with DeltaY and horizontally with DeltaX. |
| Element origin | Turns the wheel over the center of the element named by OnElement. |
| Viewport origin | Turns the wheel at an X and Y position of the viewport when the rule has no element. |
| Real wheel events | Raises the wheel events of the page, unlike a scroll made by a script. |
| Loop element | Scrolls the current element of a for-each loop when the rule names none. |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case | Description |
| Inner lists | Scroll a list or a table that has its own scroll bar. |
| Lazy loading | Scroll down until a page loads its next items. |
| Maps and charts | Zoom a map or a chart that reacts to the wheel. |
| Horizontal content | Scroll a carousel or a wide table sideways. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case | Description |
| Wheel handlers | Verify that a page reacts to wheel events, such as a zoom or a sticky header. |
| Infinite scroll | Verify that more items load when a list reaches its end. |
| Scroll containers | Verify that the wheel scrolls the element it turns over and not the page. |

edge_cases: Page is already at its end
annotations.expected_result: The page scrolls down by 600 pixels.
annotations.notes: The step runs only inside InvokeInputActions. A negative DeltaY scrolls up.

description: ### Scroll the page down
The DeltaY parameter turns the wheel 600 pixels down.
Without an element the wheel turns at the top-left corner of the viewport, which scrolls the page.

annotations.expected_result: The list scrolls down by 400 pixels and loads its next items.
annotations.notes: The element must be inside the viewport, or the driver rejects the sequence. Scroll the page to the element first when needed.

description: ### Scroll a list that has its own scroll bar
The `onElement` value names the list with an XPath.
The wheel turns 400 pixels down over the center of the list, so the list scrolls and the page stays.

edge_cases: No scrollable content under the position
annotations.expected_result: The content under that point scrolls 300 pixels to the right.
annotations.notes: A position selects which scrollable area receives the wheel. Positions depend on the window size, so set it first when a flow relies on them.

description: ### Scroll sideways at a position in the viewport
DeltaX turns the wheel 300 pixels to the right.
X and Y place the wheel 400 pixels from the left edge and 300 pixels from the top edge of the viewport.

edge_cases: Element is already at its start
annotations.expected_result: The chat history scrolls up by 250 pixels and shows earlier messages.
annotations.notes: Use the Locator to choose how the element is found. A negative amount scrolls up or left.

description: ### Scroll up inside an element found with a CSS selector
The element is found with a CSS selector.
A negative DeltaY turns the wheel 250 pixels up over its center.
Sets how far the wheel scrolls horizontally, in pixels.
A positive value scrolls right and a negative value scrolls left.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: DeltaX

description: Sets how far the wheel scrolls vertically, in pixels.
A positive value scrolls down and a negative value scrolls up.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: DeltaY

description: Sets the horizontal place of the wheel, in pixels.
With a named or inherited element it is an offset from the element center; otherwise it is measured from the left edge of the viewport.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: X

description: Sets the vertical place of the wheel, in pixels.
With a named or inherited element it is an offset from the element center; otherwise it is measured from the top edge of the viewport.
Defaults to 0, and text that is not a whole number fails the step.
parameters.name: Y

description: Holds the parameters of the scroll, such as `{{$ --DeltaY:600}}`.
A rule without an argument adds a scroll of zero pixels, which changes nothing.
properties.name: Argument

description: Selects how the OnElement value finds the element to scroll.
Accepted values include Xpath, CssSelector, Id, LinkText, and PartialLinkText.
Defaults to Xpath, and is read only when OnElement is set.
properties.name: Locator

description: Names the element the wheel turns over, in the form the Locator selects.
The wheel turns at the center of the element, shifted by X and Y when they are set.
An element that is not found fails the step, and the container then sends nothing.
The element is found before the sequence is sent, so it must already be in the page; inside a for-each loop the search starts from the loop element.
properties.name: OnElement

summary: Adds a wheel scroll to the sequence of its InvokeInputActions container.
Turns the wheel by a number of pixels down, up, right, or left, from the center of an element or from a position in the viewport.
Sends real wheel input, so pages that load content or zoom on wheel events react as they do for a person.
